_about: The guarantees of 1939 the declare-war card names, and the game keeps (ruling 229, part 3, from the historian's facts: /mnt/project-files/historian/ruling-229-facts.md, section 3). Each runs one way: the great power comes in for the small country, never the reverse, and none of them is a friendship (relations.json keeps those, for opinion and the League). In the grand campaign, when a country is attacked by a power its guarantee covered, each guarantor run by the computer declares war on the attacker the same day, as a mother country standing by a dominion does: it declares nothing else by it, and a country outside both blocs stays outside. A guarantor the player leads is never forced: he is told, and the Declare war card is his. 'against' is a list of the powers covered, 'any' for every power, or 'europe' for every power whose capital is in Europe. 'from' and 'to' are the months the guarantee stood (Romania renounced its guarantee on 1 July 1940, month 11). A guarantee ends with its guarantor's fall (France's at its armistice), and a guaranteed country that has joined another alliance than its guarantor's when it is attacked has none (one in the League of small nations keeps its guarantees). 'consult' marks a guarantee that bound its guarantor against any other power only to consult: Poland's protocol bound Britain and France against Germany alone (the Soviet march of 17 September 1939 brought no war). The words are the UI director's (ui-director/words-guarantees-229.md): 'tie' is what the guarantee is, the start of the card's line for each guarantor, whose end 'clauses' gives as it stands for the player looking ('comes', 'war', 'consult', 'free': not bound); 'keeps' is what the news says it keeps when it is honoured; 'yours' is what the news tells a player who leads the guarantor, whom it never forces. 'deter' is how much less likely a computer-run staff is to open an operation against a country a guarantor would come in for, as the League's deter is.
